??? question "In the call `add(3, 4)`, what are `3` and `4` called?"

    Arguments. Each one supplies the value for one parameter, and their number and types must match the parameter list.

    Introduced in [7. Declarations](10-declarations.md). Specification: [5. Expressions](../specification/expressions.md#calls).

??? question "Why does `2 + 3 * 4` evaluate to 14 and not 20?"

    Because of precedence. `*` groups before `+`, so the expression means `2 + (3 * 4)`.

    Introduced in [5. Expressions](08-expressions.md). Specification: [5. Expressions](../specification/expressions.md#52-precedence-and-associativity).

??? question "What do we call a piece of code that produces a value, such as `2 + 3` or `square(4.0)`?"

    An expression. A statement, by contrast, does something and produces no value.

    Introduced in [5. Expressions](08-expressions.md). Specification: [5. Expressions](../specification/expressions.md#51-expression-forms).

??? question "What is one size in an array type such as `[f32; 4, 8]` called, and when must it be known?"

    A dimension. Each one must evaluate at compile time to an integer that fits `usize`.

    Introduced in [4. Variables and types](04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [7. Arrays and shapes](../specification/arrays.md#72-dimension-rules).

??? question "What must the operand of `&` or `&mut` be, and why is `a + b` not allowed?"

    Addressable, meaning it names real storage such as a variable, field or array element; `a + b` is only a temporary result.

    Introduced in [4. Variables and types](04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [9. References and mutability](../specification/references.md#92-reference-expressions).

??? question "What do we call a variable declared with `let` inside a function?"

    A local variable. It needs an initializer and is visible from its declaration to the end of its block.

    Introduced in [4. Variables and types](04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [3. Programs and declarations](../specification/declarations.md#35-local-variable-declarations).

??? question "What is `matrix[row, column]` an example of, and what must its indices be?"

    Indexing. There must be one integer index for each dimension of the array.

    Introduced in [5. Expressions](08-expressions.md). Specification: [7. Arrays and shapes](../specification/arrays.md#76-indexing).

??? question "What do we call a piece of code that does something, such as `return x;`, and does it produce a value in Vortex?"

    A statement. In Vortex a statement produces no value.

    Introduced in [6. Statements](09-statements.md). Specification: [6. Statements and control flow](../specification/statements.md#61-statement-forms).

??? question "What do we call a named, typed input listed in a function's declaration?"

    A parameter. Every v0.1 parameter needs an explicit type and is visible only inside its function body.

    Introduced in [7. Declarations](10-declarations.md). Specification: [3. Programs and declarations](../specification/declarations.md#32-functions).

??? question "What is the result of evaluating an expression called, and how many types does it have?"

    A value. Every value has exactly one Vortex type.

    Introduced in [5. Expressions](08-expressions.md). Specification: [12. Glossary](../specification/glossary.md).

??? question "What do braces with statements inside form, and what does each one create?"

    A block. Every block creates a new scope, so a variable declared inside it cannot be used after the closing brace.

    Introduced in [6. Statements](09-statements.md). Specification: [6. Statements and control flow](../specification/statements.md#62-blocks).

??? question "In `let height: usize = 64;`, what is the `: usize` part called, and when may you leave it out?"

    A type annotation. You may leave it out of a local variable declaration when the type can be inferred from the initializer.

    Introduced in [4. Variables and types](04-variables-and-types.md).

??? question "What does `fn add(left: i32, right: i32) -> i32 { ... }` declare, and when does its body run?"

    A function. Its body runs only when code calls it, or, for `main`, when the program starts.

    Introduced in [7. Declarations](10-declarations.md). Specification: [3. Programs and declarations](../specification/declarations.md#32-functions).

??? question "What is `square(4.0)` an example of, and what happens when it runs?"

    A function call. The function's body runs, then execution carries on from just after the call.

    Introduced in [5. Expressions](08-expressions.md). Specification: [5. Expressions](../specification/expressions.md#calls).

??? question "Which statement changes the value of an existing variable, and what must be true of its target?"

    An assignment. Its target must be mutable storage, such as a variable declared with `mut`.

    Introduced in [6. Statements](09-statements.md). Specification: [6. Statements and control flow](../specification/statements.md#64-assignment).

??? question "What is it called when the same name is declared twice in one scope, and is it ever allowed?"

    A duplicate declaration. Vortex always rejects it.

    Introduced in [7. Declarations](10-declarations.md). Specification: [3. Programs and declarations](../specification/declarations.md#36-scopes).

??? question "How do you convert `count` to an `f32` in Vortex, and what is this called?"

    With a cast written like a call, `f32(count)`. A value that does not fit the new type is reported as an error rather than silently changed.

    Introduced in [5. Expressions](08-expressions.md). Specification: [4. Types and values](../specification/types-and-values.md#412-casts-and-conversions).

??? question "What do we call a value written directly in the source, such as `42` or `true`?"

    A literal. Integer, floating-point, boolean, character and string literals are the scalar forms.

    Introduced in [5. Expressions](08-expressions.md). Specification: [2. Lexical structure](../specification/lexical-structure.md#25-literals).

??? question "What is it called when an inner block redeclares a name that an outer block already declares, and does v0.1 allow it?"

    Shadowing. Whether Vortex allows it is not yet decided, so do not rely on it.

    Introduced in [7. Declarations](10-declarations.md). Specification: [3. Programs and declarations](../specification/declarations.md#36-scopes).

??? question "What do we call the number of dimensions of an array, such as 2 for `[f32; 2, 3]`?"

    Its rank. An indexing expression must give one index for each dimension.

    Introduced in [5. Expressions](08-expressions.md). Specification: [7. Arrays and shapes](../specification/arrays.md#75-rank-and-shape).

??? question "What do you declare to group related values into a new named type, such as `Point` with `x` and `y`?"

    A struct. Declaring it creates a type; a struct expression creates a value of that type.

    Introduced in [4. Variables and types](04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [8. Structs](../specification/structs.md#81-declaration).

??? question "In `let width = 128;`, what is the expression after `=` called?"

    The initializer. It gives the variable its first value and, if no type is written, its type; v0.1 requires one.

    Introduced in [4. Variables and types](04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [3. Programs and declarations](../specification/declarations.md#35-local-variable-declarations).

??? question "When a block sits inside another block, which names can each one see?"

    The inner block is a nested scope. It sees the outer names, but the outer code cannot see names declared inside it.

    Introduced in [7. Declarations](10-declarations.md). Specification: [3. Programs and declarations](../specification/declarations.md#36-scopes).

??? question "Which values does the range `0..4` produce, and how do you include the end value?"

    The values 0, 1, 2 and 3; the end is excluded. Writing `0..=4` includes the end value.

    Introduced in [5. Expressions](08-expressions.md). Specification: [5. Expressions](../specification/expressions.md#58-ranges).

??? question "In `index < 4 && values[index] > 0.0`, what stops the array read when `index` is too large?"

    Short-circuit evaluation. The right side of `&&` or `||` runs only when the left side has not already decided the answer.

    Introduced in [5. Expressions](08-expressions.md). Specification: [5. Expressions](../specification/expressions.md#57-logical-expressions).

??? question "In `struct Point { x: f32, y: f32 }`, what are `x` and `y` called, and how do you read one?"

    Fields. You read one through a value with a dot, as in `point.x`.

    Introduced in [7. Declarations](10-declarations.md). Specification: [8. Structs](../specification/structs.md#84-field-access).

??? question "What is the region of source text where a declaration's name can be used called?"

    Its scope. A local variable's scope runs from its declaration to the end of its block.

    Introduced in [7. Declarations](10-declarations.md). Specification: [3. Programs and declarations](../specification/declarations.md#36-scopes).

??? question "What check makes sure `values[index]` stays inside the array, and when does it happen?"

    A bounds check. It happens during compilation when the index is already known, and at run time otherwise.

    Introduced in [5. Expressions](08-expressions.md). Specification: [7. Arrays and shapes](../specification/arrays.md#76-indexing).

??? question "In `[f32; 4]`, what is `f32` called?"

    The element type, the single type shared by every element of the array.

    Introduced in [4. Variables and types](04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [7. Arrays and shapes](../specification/arrays.md#71-array-types).

??? question "In `for index in 0..4 { ... }`, what is `index`, and where can it be used?"

    The loop variable. It is visible only inside the loop's body.

    Introduced in [6. Statements](09-statements.md). Specification: [6. Statements and control flow](../specification/statements.md#68-for-loops).

??? question "What do we call a place in the program that introduces a name, such as `let width = 128;`?"

    A declaration. Top-level declarations are functions and structs; locals are declared by statements inside blocks.

    Introduced in [7. Declarations](10-declarations.md). Specification: [3. Programs and declarations](../specification/declarations.md#31-program-structure).

??? question "What kind of type is written as a plain name, such as `Point`, and must be matched to a struct declaration?"

    A named type. Name resolution finds the struct declaration it refers to.

    Introduced in [4. Variables and types](04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [4. Types and values](../specification/types-and-values.md#411-type-equality).
